is a comprehension method originally created as a study skill strategy for college students.
Standard Deviation
 indicates how spread out the scores are, but it is expressed in the same units as the original scores.
Standardized tests
 are constructed by test experts and used over a period of years; are designed to measure broad objectives; and, are administered using uniform procedures.
Status
 refers to the position a person occupies in a society by virtue of his age, birth, sex, marriage, occupation, achievement.
Study reading
 is done to get full understanding of the main ideas and their relationship; may involve using some other kinds of reading and/or taking down notes.
Subject-Centered Curriculum
 regards learning primarily as cognitive development and the acquisition of knowledge and information. Thus, the content is taught in isolation with no attempt at integration.
Subjectivism
 is a doctrine which determines the moral quality of an act in view of the subject, the self, or the person performing it. 
Subject Matter
 refers to the substance of teaching.
Summative Assessment
 refers to the assessment of learning after the instruction.
Synectics
 refer to how students formulate analogies in analyzing learning situations for new ideas and solutions.
Synthesis
 is the ability to put component parts together in a new different way.
Table of Specification (TOS)
 is a two-dimensional matrix that assists a teacher in determining the total number of items to construct for a long test, like periodic test.
Taoism
 advocates simplicity, frugality, and the joys of being close to nature and being in harmony with the whole universe.
Task
 refers to the activities that teachers ask students to perform to enable the students to meet the lesson objective.
Taxonomy
 is classification system that enables educators to precisely organize learning objective in an effort to achieve specific outcomes.
Teaching
 is an art of creating learning in a spontaneous manner by combining individual pieces of education and experience into new whole that is specifically made for the circumstances they see in their situation; is a science that uses specific methods and skills that will help achieve its goals (Gagne, 1970).
Teaching Approach
 refers to the teacher’s viewpoint toward the process of learning.
Teaching Method
 refers to the regular ways or orderly procedures employed by the teachers and the principles needed to accomplish the aims of learning situations.
Teaching Models
 refer to the prescriptive teaching strategies designed to accomplish
 particular instructional goals.
Teaching Strategy
 refers to the general design of how the teacher will attack her lesson.
Teaching Style
 refers to the expressive aspect of teaching, the way teachers teach, which includes their mannerisms complemented by their choices of teaching behaviors and strategies (Kellough, 2003).
Teaching Technique
 refers to the act, style or manner of performance of the teacher in carrying out the procedures or acts of teaching.
Team Teaching
 is tapping the expertise of two or more teachers in planning, teaching, and evaluating student’s learning.
Technology
 (1) refers to the systematic application of scientific or other organized body of knowledge to practical tasks; (2) It refers to the physical equipment, facilities, (hardware) and the programs or modular materials that result from the application of technological process.
Technology of Education
 is synonymous to educational technology whose thrust is tied with the learning process, and whose important aspect is the software part of technology, that is , the design of teaching and learning situations that enhance and facilitate learning in general.
Teleology
 tries to elucidate whether or not there is a purpose in the universe.
Tests
 are 
used as tools for measuring the knowledge, skills, and attitudes of learners.

They 
may vary according to function, content, form, administration procedures, scoring system, and interpretation.
Thematic Approach
 is a teaching approach that organizes subject matter around unifying themes.
Theoretical Education
 is learning higher forms of learning skills such as religion, values, music, literary and social knowledge.
Thinking
 is the ability to analyze, criticize, and reach conclusions based on sound reference or judgment

(Arends, 2004).
Think-Pair Strategy
 is done when the teacher poses a question or issue regarding the lesson in which the students will spend time thinking for the answer. Each student talks about the answer to a partner and shares each other’s ideas. Each pair will be given the chance to report to class what they have discussed. 
Transformative Education
 is an educational process that brings about deep and significant changes (for the better) in an individual and ultimately culminates in similar changes at the societal level, principally brought about through innovative and creative teaching and learning, curriculum reform and appropriate policy at the school level.
Time Allotment
 refers to the amount of time available for the lesson.
Transfer of Learning
 occurs when a person’s learning in one situation influences his learning and performance in other situations.
Tree Outline
 is a planning tool that helps the reader analyze the story so that the questions during discussion will create a coherent framework for understanding text.
Understanding by Design (UbD
) is the teaching method that gives more stress on the 
why 
rather than on the 
what
. This is in line with the current curricular reform that addresses emphasis on understanding of the knowledge acquired. 
This was developed by Jay Mc Tighe and Grant Wiggins.
Utilitarianism
 maximizes the usefulness of every individual to the goals of general worth to others or to state.
Validity 
is one important criterion of a good assessment instrument which means it should measure what it intends to measure.
Values
 are bedrock beliefs that give direction to a person’s life. These are convictions so deeply rooted that they prompt individuals to prize them, cherish them, and act consistently in ways that are congruent with them (Savage and Armstrong, 1982).
Value Clarification
 refers to the cluster of instructional strategies that involves students working collaboratively to clarify set of values.
Venn Diagram
 is a graphic organizer in which two or more overlapping circles help develop the thinking skill of comparing and contrasting.
Visual Aids
 refer to any device used to aid in the communication of idea.
Visual Learners
 must see their teacher’s actions and facial expression to fully understand the content of the lesson.
Visual Perception
 is critical to the reading and writing processes as it addresses the ability to notice important details and assign meaning to what is seen.
Wait Time
 refers to the pauses between the teacher’s pauses questions, the students’ response, and other teacher’s reaction. 
With-it-ness
 is one of the characteristics of an effective classroom manager. One sign of this is awareness of what’s happening in all parts of the classroom.
